title: sutra_dead: detect Rust test exemptions and FFI entrypoints
description:
sutra_dead against a real Rust crate (chitta) reports 200 dead symbols, of which approximately 85 percent are test functions inside cfg-test mod blocks plus integration tests in tests/. The tool's own response advertises this as a known limitation. Every consumer of sutra_dead has to reinvent the same filter.

Surfaced during chitta release-review spike, 2026-05-08. The dead-code report was so noisy I had to manually filter it before handing it to a code-review subagent.

Symptoms:
- Functions inside cfg-test mod blocks reported dead. Their callers are sibling test functions discovered by Cargo at test-binary link time, not by sutra's call graph.
- tests/contract.rs and tests/integration.rs reported as "unreachable files". They are integration tests reachable via Cargo test target sections in Cargo.toml, not via mod imports.
- FFI entrypoints (no_mangle, wasm_bindgen, pyo3 macros) similarly cannot be detected as live by symbol-graph reachability alone.

Fix sketch:
- Walk attributes on each function/module symbol; treat the test, tokio-test, async-test, bench attributes as reachability roots.
- Treat any item inside a cfg-test module as test-exempt.
- Parse Cargo.toml test and bench target sections; the named files are reachability roots for integration tests.
- Walk attributes for FFI exemptions: no_mangle, unsafe-no_mangle, wasm_bindgen, pyo3 attribute macros.

acceptance_criteria.text: Test attributes (test, tokio test, async test, bench) treated as reachability roots; their attributed functions and transitive callees are live
Items inside cfg-test modules treated as test-exempt
Files declared in Cargo.toml test and bench target sections treated as reachable
FFI exemption attributes (no_mangle, wasm_bindgen, pyo3 etc) mark their symbols as live entrypoints
Re-run sutra_dead on chitta workspace: under 20 entries (down from 200)
Tool description still discloses any remaining exemption gaps it cannot detect
